name: python-dropped-import-still-called-asks
desc: removing `from ulid import ULID` while the new text still calls ULID() is the obs-py-002 pattern → ask. The additive check stays silent here because addInFileDefs folds the OLD on-disk file's import into the known set — proving this ask comes from dropped-import, not the additive check

name: python-dropped-import-removed-and-unused-clean
desc: the import AND every use are gone — a legitimate cleanup, stays silent

name: js-dropped-import-still-used-asks
desc: a removed named JS import still called below → ask
old:
import { fetchUser } from './api';
const u = fetchUser(id);

name: go-dropped-import-excluded-clean
desc: Go is excluded by design (imports are used package-qualified, so a dropped Go import surfaces as a qualified reference handled elsewhere). The exclusion itself lives in the pure function, so what this case adds is that the whole hook pipeline — LangFor, the pre-edit file read, hookOldLines/hookAddedLines — stays silent on a Go file whose import was removed while a qualified use remains, rather than some other check firing in its place
